mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of UBO's home jurisdiction (e.g., IRCC for Canadian passports) and a notary public in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the executing jurisdiction is a Hague Convention member state; otherwise consular legalization at the Canadian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Director Consent to Act (Alberta Form 2 / individual consent) executed by each proposed director and UBO appointee
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Alberta Corporate Registry (filed with Articles of Incorporation); notarized and apostilled when executed outside Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Source-of-Funds Certification for each UBO (counter-party due diligence)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, UBOs, and authorized signatories against (i) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA); (ii) Canada's Criminal Code s. 83.05 listed terrorist entities; (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List required for USD clearing and Apple/Google payment rails; and (v) PEP identification per PCMLTFA s. 9.3 with enhanced due diligence (EDD) for heads of state, cabinet-level officials, military commanders, senior judiciary, and family/close associates. Given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier for simulated social casino publishing, EDD is mandatory at onboarding, with ongoing transaction monitoring and registry refresh at least annually and upon any UBO change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES / online corporate registration system) operated by Service Alberta, with mandatory NUANS (National Unified Automated Name Search) priority search filed through authorized corporate registry agents
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta corporate names must be expressed in English or French (or a combined English/French form) using the Latin alphabet; names using non-Roman scripts must be fully transliterated or romanized; punctuation, symbols, and numerals are restricted to permitted characters under the Alberta Business Corporations Act and regulations; the legal element ('Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Incorporated', 'Limited') must be included; the name must contain a distinctive element plus a descriptive or geographic element to satisfy the distinctiveness rule
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant shall, within 30 days, file a written Request for Reconsideration with the Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry, supported by a fresh NUANS report, a sworn affidavit of distinctiveness, and any required ministerial or regulator consent letters (e.g., AGLC consent or non-objection for 'Casino'/'Gaming'-type tokens). If the Registrar sustains the refusal, the applicant may apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review under the Judicature Act, or alternatively incorporate under a different cleared name and subsequently amend the corporate name by Articles of Amendment once the desired name is released.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is permissible for the statutory registered office in Alberta provided the address is a physical street address in Alberta capable of accepting service of process and is not a P.O. Box; the company must maintain a separate records office within Alberta where corporate records, the shareholder register, and the UBO register are kept. For a social casino software publisher with no real-money wagering licence, a virtual office satisfies incorporation and CRA/GST registration requirements, but the directors' records-keeping and oversight duties remain in force.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: ~5–10% within the first 12 months: CRA random audit or residency verification and banking/merchant KYC site-visit requirements present a quantified low-to-moderate inspection risk; AGLC physical inspection is not applicable absent licensed real-money gambling activity, provided the platform strictly operates on simulated play with no cash payouts.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, including sections 5-7 on incorporation, sections 102-117 on directors and officers, sections 118-123 on corporate proceedings, and applicable provisions concerning registered office, records, shares, and corporate filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, administered through Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Alberta Corporate Registry Form 1), accompanied by Notice of Address (Form 3), Notice of Directors (Form 4), and Notice of Agent for Service (Form 2), where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. Shares may be issued for consideration approved by the directors, subject to the Alberta Business Corporations Act. Alberta does not require a statutory escrow account for incorporation capital. The corporation must maintain adequate records of issued shares, subscriptions, consideration received, and stated capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Corporation accept and record the subscription for the shares described in the subscription agreement, for the consideration stated therein, subject to receipt of that consideration. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office and records office stated in the incorporation filings are adopted as the Corporation’s offices until changed by the directors. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the persons identified in the incorporation documents are appointed as directors and officers in the capacities stated therein, with authority to execute banking, tax, employment, technology, and commercial documents for the Corporation. The officers shall maintain all statutory registers and filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Corporate Name and Registered Agent Arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry service provider or authorized registry agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select either a numbered corporation or a distinctive named corporation. For a named corporation, obtain the required Alberta name search or NUANS report through an authorized registry agent. Confirm an Alberta registered office, records office, and Alberta agent for service where required. Verify that the proposed name does not conflict with an existing corporation or regulated name.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-company request
Name search or NUANS report, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an amended name, a new search report, or use a numbered corporation. If an address or agent filing is rejected, correct the address, obtain the required consent, and resubmit through the registry agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry online services or an authorized Alberta registry agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Articles of Incorporation and the related notices. State the corporation name, share structure, restrictions on share transfers, number of directors or director range, and any prescribed restrictions. Submit the filing electronically or through a registry agent and pay the applicable fee in Canadian dollars. No general notarization is required for standard Alberta incorporation filings; certified or notarized documents may be requested for identity, authority, or foreign-party verification.
required_dossiers: Notice of Agent for Service, Form 2, if applicable
Name search or NUANS documentation, if applicable
Applicable filing fee in Canadian dollars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For a deficiency notice, correct the identified statutory form, name, address, director, or share-structure defect and resubmit through the same registry channel. Preserve the filing receipt and request written clarification from the registry agent where the notice is ambiguous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate and Establish Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry for the certificate; the corporation and its records office for internal records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, certified Articles, corporate access number, and filed notices. Prepare the minute book, securities register, register of directors and officers, register of shareholders, share certificates or uncertificated share records, incorporator declaration, and initial resolutions. Record the registered office, records office, fiscal year-end, banking authority, and beneficial ownership information.
required_dossiers: Share certificates or electronic securities records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or filed documents contain an error, contact the registry agent promptly and file an amendment, correction, or replacement document as permitted. Maintain an audit trail linking the corrected document to the original filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Approve Share Issuance and Corporate Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation’s board of directors and shareholders where shareholder approval is legally or constitutionally required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board resolution, approve the share subscription and consideration, appoint officers, authorize banking and contracts, confirm the registered and records offices, and approve accounting and fiscal-year policies. Issue shares only after the agreed consideration is received or properly recorded. Maintain director conflict disclosures and comply with applicable notice, quorum, and meeting requirements.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a resolution is defective, reconvene the board with proper notice and quorum, ratify the action where legally permissible, and correct the securities register. Obtain shareholder approval where the Act, Articles, or unanimous shareholder agreement requires it.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Payroll, and Federal Regulatory Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Employment and Social Development Canada, and relevant Alberta authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a CRA Business Number and register for corporate income tax, GST/HST where applicable, payroll, and import or export accounts where relevant. Register for Alberta Workers’ Compensation Board coverage if the corporation employs workers in covered industries. Assess privacy, consumer protection, online marketing, copyright, and platform terms applicable to digital game publishing. No gambling licence should be assumed if the product is purely virtual and provides no cash or cash-equivalent prizes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax or payroll registration is queried, provide incorporation documents, ownership information, business-activity details, and identity verification. Correct the application and preserve the CRA or provincial reference number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Verify Municipal Premises and Digital-Operations Requirements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal business licensing office, municipal planning and development authority, Alberta Occupational Health and Safety authorities, and applicable platform operators.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the corporation operates from physical premises, confirm municipal zoning, business licensing, occupancy, signage, fire, and building requirements before occupancy. For a remote or office-only digital publishing operation, document the premises assessment and retain platform, privacy, cybersecurity, and consumer-law compliance records. Obtain separate advice before adding wagering, cash prizes, paid-entry contests, or regulated gaming mechanics.
required_dossiers: Fire and building inspection records, if applicable
Privacy policy and terms of service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a municipality identifies an unlicensed use or zoning issue, suspend occupancy or the affected activity, obtain the required licence or variance, and submit revised premises information. If gaming mechanics create regulated gambling exposure, obtain specialized Alberta gaming-law advice before launch.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry and the applicable municipal licensing, planning, building, fire, and occupational health and safety authorities. No general Alberta industrial licensing board is ordinarily applicable to a software publisher conducting simulated social casino or virtual slots game publishing without real-money wagering.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general Alberta manufacturing or industrial operating permit for software publishing. A municipal business licence, zoning approval, occupancy permit, or fire inspection may be required based on the physical premises and municipality.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for ordinary office-based digital publishing and software distribution with no industrial facility, resource activity, material processing, or significant emissions. Project-specific screening is required if the business later develops a data centre, industrial facility, power installation, or waste-generating operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No sector-specific wastewater, VOC, or industrial-emissions thresholds ordinarily apply to an office-based game publisher. Any wastewater discharge, hazardous materials, electronic waste, fuel storage, generators, or industrial emissions must comply with applicable Alberta environmental legislation, municipal bylaws, waste-management requirements, and approved discharge or handling conditions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For ordinary leased office premises, confirm municipal occupancy, fire-code, emergency-egress, and building requirements with the municipality and obtain any required inspection or business licence. No industrial structural-load clearance is ordinarily required beyond the building owner’s approvals. The employer must comply with Alberta Occupational Health and Safety legislation, including hazard assessment, emergency procedures, workplace training, and incident reporting. Additional electrical, fire, structural, and occupational approvals are required for server rooms, generators, workshops, warehouses, or other specialized facilities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); federal portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-business-portal.html). Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA under the Canada–Alberta Tax Collection Agreement; Alberta has no separate corporate tax administration for registration purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Resident Business Corporation (incorporated federally under CBCA or provincially under Alberta Business Corporations Act): CRA automatically issues a 9-digit Business Number (BN) upon incorporation registration. The BN serves as the statutory taxpayer identifier; corporate income tax (RC program account), GST/HST (RT program account) and payroll (RP) accounts are opened through CRA Business Registration (Form RC1 or online via My Business Account). Foreign entity without Canadian incorporation: must file Form RC1 to obtain a BN and register RC/RT/RP program accounts if it carries on business in Canada; a non-resident digital-services supplier with no Canadian establishment must use the CRA simplified non-resident GST/HST registration portal where Canadian digital-supply turnover exceeds CAD 30,000 in a 12-month period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Canadian law. A Canadian Business Corporation is mandatorily classified as a separate taxpayer taxing worldwide income at the entity level. Hybrid mismatch rules apply under Income Tax Act s. 18.4 (hybrid financial instruments and hybrid transfer arrangements) and s. 212(1)(b) Part XIII withholding on hybrid surpluses. Functional elections include: CCPC-status designations under ss. 125(6)-(7) and s. 256(1.1) (non-resident-owned control prevention), s. 112 inter-corporate dividend deduction (automatic for taxable Canadian corporations; disallowed for hybrid surplus), safe-harbour elections under tax treaties for permanent-establishment attribution, and the foreign affiliate surplus/grifter computations under s. 5907 for outbound foreign subsidiaries. For ISIC 5820 social-casino publishers, no patent or IP box incentive exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); Alberta applies 5% federal GST only, with no Alberta provincial sales tax or HST component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic small supplier rule: CAD 30,000 of taxable worldwide supplies in any trailing 12-month period (s. 148 ETA). Digital economy mandatory registration for non-resident electronic-commerce suppliers: taxable supplies of digital goods and services to Canadian-resident recipients exceeding CAD 30,000 in a 12-month period trigger mandatory GST/HST registration (effective July 1, 2021 framework). A Canadian-resident Business Corporation publishing simulated social casino and virtual slots software must register for GST/HST once its taxable supplies (including Apple IAP/Google Play Billing sales) exceed the CAD 30,000 threshold; registration is also mandatory where the person makes taxable supplies in Canada and is engaged in a commercial activity in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or pre-clearance electronic invoicing mandates. However: (i) GST/HST registrants must maintain adequate books and records substantiating commercial activity and zero-rated exports (s. 286 ETA); (ii) electronic filing of GST/HST returns is mandatory for registrants with gross annual revenue exceeding CAD 1,500,000 and for most corporations; (iii) T2 corporate income tax returns must be filed electronically for corporations with gross revenues exceeding CAD 1,000,000; (iv) CRA requires platform operators (Apple, Google) to report Canadian-resident sales through statutory information requests, and invoices must display the Business Number and GST/HST status; no specific API clearance or fiscal-stamping standard is prescribed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Digital games and virtual slots software delivered by wire/electronic transmission qualify for zero-rating under paragraph 23(2) (intangible personal property supplied to a non-resident) and section 25.1 (services provided to a non-resident) of Part V, Schedule VI, Excise Tax Act, provided (i) the recipient is a non-resident at the time of the supply, (ii) delivery occurs electronically to a destination outside Canada, and (iii) the consideration does not relate to a supply consumed in Canada. Social casino in-app credits and simulated slots purchases routed through Apple IAP/Google Play Billing are zero-rated only where the storefront country code, IP geolocation logs and platform settlement reports confirm non-resident end users. Zero-rating is denied where a Canadian-resident user consumes the digital content while in Canada, where the service is connected to a Canadian permanent establishment or domestic server infrastructure, or where post-sale live-ops support is rendered in Canada. Physical exports of gaming servers or hardware qualify for zero-rating under s. 2, Part V, Schedule VI subject to customs documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canada Customs Export Declaration (G7/CAED via ARC or EDE portal) - required for physical goods export
Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing cross-border movement of physical goods
Commercial invoice describing the digital supply and identifying the non-resident recipient (Apple App Store Connect / Google Play Console payout statements accepted for marketplace digital sales)
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-exchange contract proving receipt of external consideration within the repatriation window
Non-resident status evidence pack: foreign tax identification number, residency declaration, IP-address routing logs, and platform storefront country code
GST/HST sales ledger segregating zero-rated export supplies (Schedule 5 code 0-5)
Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlement reports showing non-Canadian storefront sales and FX conversion
Server access or download logs indicating delivery to foreign IP addresses outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA actively audits digital-publishing and casual-gaming companies under its E-Services and Digital Economy compliance program. Zero-rating claims lacking documented non-resident delivery are reassessed to add 5% GST plus arrears interest. Civil penalties: s. 280(1) ETA false-statement penalty equal to 25% of the tax understated (minimum CAD 500); s. 280(2) gross-negligence penalty equal to the greater of CAD 4,000 and 50% of the tax sought to be evaded. Criminal prosecution for wilful evasion under s. 327 ETA carries, on summary conviction, a fine of up to CAD 50,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 2 years, and on indictment, a fine of up to CAD 200,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years. The CRA may reassess beyond the normal 4-year limitation period where misrepresentation, neglect, or wilful default is established, and indefinitely in cases of fraud. Refund set-off and deemed-trust rules (s. 222 ETA) authorize the CRA to withhold zero-rating refunds pending export-documentation compliance and to claw back refunds paid in error with accruing interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility for the Canadian dollar. There are no exchange-control laws, no foreign-exchange approval requirements, and no restrictions on profit remittances, dividend distributions, or capital repatriation for non-resident shareholders, provided that the underlying corporate filings, tax-cleared distribution documentation, and AML-driven source-of-funds verification are in order. For a non-resident-controlled Business Corporation carrying on digital software publishing in Alberta, all profits generated from international sales may be freely converted and remitted to the parent enterprise; the only practical hurdles are standard bank-level compliance screening for the virtual-gaming sector and the requirement to evidence beneficial ownership and source of funds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement. There is no mandatory timeline or minimum conversion ratio; export receipts earned in foreign currency may be retained in the original currency, converted at commercial rates, or held in assigned eligible deposit accounts. The Canadian reporting obligations are limited to statistical and AML reporting — specifically, certain incoming and outgoing international wire transfers and transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 must be reported to the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) and, where applicable, to Statistics Canada under the International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High with legal constraints. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) may be used only as paymentaggregator and foreign-currency clearing gateways, but they cannot maintain Canadian-dollar deposit-taking operations or provide banking services in Canada without a Canadian bank charter or a registered Money Services Business (MSB) authorization under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. An offshore EMI operating without Canadian licensing cannot legally open domestic clearing accounts or receive CDN settlement rails. For this cross-border social-casino publishing entity, the offshore EMI may serve as a supplementary collection vehicle for Apple IAP and Google Play billing remittances, provided all funds are swept to a licensed Canadian operational account and full transactional rail visibility is maintained for FINTRAC reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most Tier 1 Canadian banks require directors and authorized signatories to attend an in-person KYC interview at a Canadian branch or to complete a video-verified notarized interview with apostilled corporate documentation. Remote opening is available for non-resident directors, but the bank will apply enhanced due diligence: verified director identity, registered office proof, certified certificate of incorporation, beneficial ownership register, and source-of-wealth statements. A physical presence is not an absolute statutory mandate, but banks may impose a physical meeting for higher-risk gaming and non-resident structures. To avoid delay, the treasury plan should designate at least one Canadian resident director or an authorized banking officer for in-branch signing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity — non-resident corporate parent with multi-tier jurisdiction layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner registry with full identity, residency, nationality, and source-of-wealth evidence; organizational chart of all intermediate holding entities; certified memorandum and articles; notarized board resolution authorizing account opening; and negative-check certification for politically exposed persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Simulated gambling / social casino sector red flag — potential unlicensed gaming exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legally binding legal opinion confirming that the platform operates as a social-casino simulation with no transferable digital tokens and no real-money wagering; developer agreements with Apple and Google showing distribution through App Store / Play Store; internal policy prohibiting real-money payout/withdrawal to players; and third-party jurisdictional gaming-law assessment for target markets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk counterparty jurisdictions in customer base or vendor ecosystem
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP address geolocation reports and transaction monitoring policy; complete vendor due-diligence files; sanctions screening procedure demonstrating OFAC / UN / Canadian sanctions compliance; and restricted-country blocking rule documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent source of capital injection for a newly incorporated Alberta entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements for the contributing parent entity covering at least 12 months; accountant-certified trail of funds; subscription agreement and share issuance ledger; Board minute approving the capital contribution; and legal invoice/property appraisal if non-cash consideration is used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high transaction velocity and international outgoing remittances to gaming suppliers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A matured treasury policy covering transaction velocity, daily settlement limits, KYC refresh cycles, approved-beneficiary whitelists, and periodic third-party AML audit attestation; contractual copies of Apple/Google settlement schedules; and a FINTRAC-compliant suspicious transaction reporting framework.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant route begins with a SWIFT MT103 wire from the parent enterprise's regulated financial institution to the Alberta Business Corporation's Capital Escrow Account at the chosen Tier 1 Canadian bank. The wire must include the exact Treasury Purpose Code 'Direct Investment into non-resident-controlled enterprise' and the domestic corporate bank's associated imputation code. The remitter must provide: (i) certified board resolution approving the equity injection, (ii) shareholder register and subscription agreement, (iii) source-of-funds documentation covering the prior 12 months, and (iv) confirmatory legal certificate of corporate existence. The receiving bank will run FINTRAC and OFAC/UN sanctions screening; once cleared, the funds are recorded as contributed surplus or share capital and remain subject to the bank's enhanced monitoring for the virtual-gaming classification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational outbound payments for trade settlements and supplier disbursements will be executed through SWIFT MT103 priority payment orders for low-value and high-frequency remittances, while larger one-off settlements for platform licensing, content acquisition, or infrastructure contracts may use a Commercial Letter of Credit with transferable and irrevocable usance terms. For the Apple IAP and Google Play Billing flows, the company will maintain a consolidated merchant settlement account via direct bank-integrated APIs or a FINTRAC-registered PSP, with daily ACH and wire sweeps into the Canadian operational account. Anti-money-laundering boundaries are enforced through beneficiary whitelisting, counterparty sanctions checks, and transaction-value limits tied to the board-approved treasury policy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (plain-vanilla, CAD/USD and CAD/EUR) with major Canadian bank counterparties
Cross-currency swaps for long-term netting and liquidity rebalancing between operating and parent entities
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) instruments only for exotic currency exposures not supported by the domestic Canadian interbank deliverable market
FX options combined with forwards for contingency hedging of virtual-goods seasonal revenue peaks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 late fee after the 60-day deadline; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including Alberta corporate income tax schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the sixth month after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% penalty on unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; interest accrues; directors may be liable for unremitted withholdings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end for annual filers (revenue ≤ CAD 1.5M)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% late-filing penalty plus 1% per month up to 12 months; interest; no corporate strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA), an independent audit is required unless the corporation meets the eligible-corporation test: gross revenue ≤ CAD 10,000,000 and total assets ≤ CAD 5,000,000 in the preceding fiscal year, and a shareholder (holding 10%+ of votes) has not demanded an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private corporations may use Canadian ASPE or IFRS; IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No public annual UBO confirmation filing exists in Alberta. The ABCA requires every corporation to maintain a Significant Individual Register (SIR) identifying individuals holding ≥25% of voting shares, control in fact, or de facto control. Updates must be made within 15 days of any change and are available to shareholders and law enforcement upon request.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $110 – $260 (registered office and corporate agent services for an Alberta corporation)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% aggregate for an Alberta-resident Business Corporation (federal general corporate rate 15.0% plus Alberta general corporate rate 8.0%); 11.0% combined rate applies to the first CA$500,000 of active business income if the corporation qualifies as a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) under ITA s.125
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal SR&ED Investment Tax Credit: 35% refundable for qualifying CCPC expenditures up to the CA$3 million expenditure limit, otherwise 15% non-refundable. Alberta Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit (25%) exists for qualifying interactive digital media products but expressly excludes products whose principal purpose is gambling or simulated gambling monetization, so social-casino software is generally ineligible. No statutory tax holidays are available at the federal or Alberta provincial level.
